title: List of bugged actions and reactions
html:
This list aims to catalogue actions and reactions which do not function as would be expected based on their tooltips, or which have other problems - or missing information - in their description, function, or location. This list is unlikely to be comprehensive as it is likely there are many issues with actions and reactions of which we are unaware.

As this list deals with problems that have a high likelihood of being changed in patches and hotfixes, it is likely that entries will be incorrect following an update.

All entries are currently correct as of Hotfix 33.

Actions and reactions

More...
Name Bugs
 Absorb Elements
  • This reaction cannot be used while affected by  Starry Form.
 Accursed Spectre (reaction)
  • The description does not state it, but this cannot be used on undead.
  • Creatures killed by  Cull the Weak will not trigger this reaction.
  • The CharacterStats for this summoned creature does not correctly have the proper DifficultyStatuses set, and as a result the creature loses 30% HP from the Explorer difficulty modifier as if it were a hostile NPC.
  • This reaction cannot be used while affected by  Starry Form or when  Disguised.
 Acid Breath
  • The tooltip incorrectly describes the area of effect as a cone, when it is instead a line.
 Arcane Shot: Beguiling Arrow
  • Due to an incorrectly used DamageBonus function, the bonus damage that Arcane Shots deliver on striking an enemy can never critically hit.
 Arcane Shot: Bursting Arrow
  • Unlike most other Arcane Shot options, this action consumes the  Arcane Arrow immediately rather than on hit. Instead, this resource cost is refunded on a miss which is almost equivalent behaviour. This results in some unusual behaviour with  Curving Shot. If Bursting Shot misses its initial target, the  Arcane Arrow cost is refunded and then the attack is redirected to a new target. If this target is hit, the Bursting Arrow will apply for effectively free. If the redirected hit also misses, it will refund yet another Arcane Arrow netting +1  Arcane Arrow in total.
 Arcane Shot: Enfeebling Arrow
  • Due to an incorrectly used DamageBonus function, the bonus damage that Arcane Shots deliver on striking an enemy can never critically hit.
 Arcane Shot: Grasping Arrow
  • Due to an incorrectly used DamageBonus function, the bonus damage that Arcane Shots receive on striking an enemy can never critically hit.
 Arcane Shot: Piercing Arrow
  • Since this attack does not involve an attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include:
    •  Arcane Synergy
    •  Gloves of Archery
    •  Hunter's Mark
    •  Sharpshooter: All In
    •  Titanstring Bow
 Arcane Shot: Seeking Arrow
  • Since this attack does not involve an attack roll, it does not benefit from certain bonus damage sources which check the attack roll type despite listing the additional damage on the tooltip. These include:
    •  Arcane Synergy
    •  Gloves of Archery
    •  Hunter's Mark
    •  Sharpshooter: All In
    •  Titanstring Bow
 Arcane Shot: Shadow Arrow
  • Due to an incorrectly used DamageBonus function, the bonus damage that Arcane Shots deliver on striking an enemy can never critically hit.
 Archer's Eye
  • In what appears to be an oversight, there are no weapons in the game which give Archer's Eye, so this weapon action is moot.
 Aspect of the Elk
  • The extra movement speed is applied when a character starts its turn in range of the effect or moves into its range. There is no limit on the number of times this can be applied on the same turn, and the extra movement speed is not removed upon leaving the effective range. A character moving very slightly into and out of range multiple times (consuming less than 1.5 m / 5 ft of movement each time) can gradually gain a theoretically unbounded amount of extra movement.
 Aura of Murder (action)
  • Despite the extra description, no restriction exists which cause creatures which cannot be Frightened to be immune to Aura of Murder.
 Awaken Crawling Claws
  • The in-game description says this action stuns enemies within 4 m / 13 ft, but the radius is significantly larger at 12 m / 40 ft.
 Backbreaker
  • This attack may only target characters that are Large size or smaller, and is missing the related tooltip warning found on similar attacks, such as  Trip Attack (Melee).
 Bardic Inspiration (class action)
  • When used to modify an attack roll with a +1d10 bonus, the Bardic Inspiration condition is not removed from the character.
  • Bardic Inspiration may target a character who is already affected by the +1d10 version, wasting the effect as they do not stack.
 Bind Hexed Weapon
  • Despite the extra description of a warlock's bound weapon returning "to its previous state", no code exists in the game which removes Hexed Weapon from a weapon that is away from the Warlock.
  • The Hexed Weapon condition is only removed on respec if the weapon is equipped while doing do; leaving the weapon in inventory does not remove it.
 Bind Pact Weapon
  • Despite the extra description, no code exists in the game that removes Pact Weapon from a weapon that is away from the Warlock.
  • The Pact Weapon condition only get removed on respec if the weapon was equipped. Leaving the weapon in inventory wont remove it.
 Bite (Bat)
  • The tooltip states this attack should apply two turns of a condition named "Weakening Infection", which is identical to  Infected but with -3 to Constitution. The attack lacks the necessary code to apply such a condition to a target.
 Bladesong
  • The requirement to be wielding a dagger, longsword, etc. applies only to the main hand. While "Bladesong Impeded" will be displayed on the Wizard, Bladesong will still be usable even if the off hand is wielding an incompatible weapon.
    • Bladesinger wizards cannot accumulate climax charges if the weapon in their offhand is not compatible, nor can they use the climax.
 Bloodlust (Redcap)
  • The version of this action used by Redcaps in the Sunlit Wetlands is not affected by  Calm Emotions, while the version used by Redcaps in The Blushing Mermaid is.
 Bolstering Magic: Level 1 Spell Slot
  • This ability cannot restore spell slots to a druid because that class is erroneously not given the technical passive UnlockedSpellSlotLevel1. The absence of this passive feature has no other impact on the druid's spellcasting ability, however. This only applies to first level slots so  Bolstering Magic: Level 2 Spell Slot and  Bolstering Magic: Level 3 Spell Slot should work properly.
 Bolt of Celestial Light
  • This action does not use Superiority Dice at any time, contrary to the in-game tooltip stating "On Miss: Does not spend Superiority Dice."
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to struck targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy.
 Boon of the Unstoppable
  • When the Bhaal cultists chant their ritual to trigger this action, it applies a bugged status condition that displays as Unstoppable but lacks any actual damage reduction. For this reason, the first damage instance each round is not reduced to 1.
  • Subsequent damage instances in the same round are properly reduced to 1 by the correct Unstoppable status condition.
 Brace (Melee)
  • When combined with other dice rerolling features, the combat log may show an incorrect number of rerolls.
 Break of Dawn
  • The tooltip incorrectly states "Targets still take half damage" when instead they are neither pushed back nor made prone.
 Bull Rush
  • The in-game tooltip is not accurate. It is duplicated from the similar  Primal Stampede ability. In particular, the tooltip says Bull Rush does damage, knocks targets prone, and is only available while  Raging, none of which are true.
 Call for Help
  • Despite what is shown in the tooltip, this action does not grant  Action Surge.
 Chalice Healing
  • When receiving this ability via Starry Form, this spell is not properly granted with Wisdom as its spellcasting modifier, and will instead use the spellcasting modifier of the most recently acquired spellcasting class.
 Challenge to Duel
  • Despite being listed as a level 1 Enchantment spell (inherited from parent spell  Compelled Duel), this action is not technically a spell (the IsSpell flag and concentration requirement from Compelled Duel has been removed). Thus, it does not interact with any spell-specific effects such as  Vivacious Cloak or  Split Enchantment.
    • It also uses weapon action DC instead of spellcasting DC and hence benefits from  Heightened Manoeuvre.
 Channel Divinity: Cloak of Shadows
  • This ability incorrectly uses the description from  Cloak of Shadows. It does not actually require the user to be obscured, and can be used in plain view of others, even in bright light.
 Charge (Deep Rothé)
  • This ability can target dead creatures, leading to unintended interactions with other on-hit effects such as  Cull the Weak.
 Charm Animals and Plants
  • This spell does not function as described, and instead acts similarly to  Charm Person. As such, and despite the lack of related tooltip warnings, this action is considered hostile by creatures that make a successful saving throw against it. The condition also ends early if the caster or an ally hurts the target, and in higher difficulty modes, the target might become hostile when the spell ends.
  • The in-game tooltip incorrectly links the default  Charmed condition instead of the condition it actually applies.
 Cinderous Swipe
  • The version of this ability granted in wild shape form deals only 1d6⁠⁠Fire extra damage, not 2d6⁠⁠Fire like the tooltip says.
 Claws (Harpy)
  • Due to how  Luring Song is coded, harpies cannot use this attack against any target that was in the Luring Song's radius when it was applied, regardless of whether the target saves against the effect or not, as long as the song continues. They can only use  Multiattack (Harpy) against such targets.
 Clench of the North Wind
  • Unlike other Way of the Four Elements actions, this still retains its HasVerbalComponent SpellFlag from its parent spell Hold Person and thus cannot be used while  Silenced.
 Click Heels
  • Due to a scripting error, the  Disadvantage component of this effect actually applies to the  Reaction attacks performed by the caster, rather than reaction attacks targeting the caster.
 Cloak of Shadows
  • Due to a poorly coded RemoveConditions field, Cloak of Shadows is lost when transitioning from a Lightly Obscured area to a Heavily Obscured area, and vice versa.
 Cloud of Jellyfish: Attack
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to struck targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy.
 Cloud of Jellyfish: Mighty Shocking Sting
  • This action cannot actually disarm a target because it applies  Disarmed instead of  Weapon Dropped!, the former of which is used as a tooltip description markup for spells which apply disarm conditions such as the latter.
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy when a target successfully rolls a saving throw against this reaction.
 Cloud of Jellyfish: Shocking Sting
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy when a target successfully rolls a saving throw against this reaction.
 Concussive Burst
  • The in-game tooltip says this attack involves a Constitution saving throw, but it actually uses an attack roll.
 Concussive Smash (Spiritual Weapon)
  • The in-game tooltip is incorrect - all the damage dealt is Force damage.
    • Contrary to other Spiritual Weapon attacks, the damage dealt is non-magical.
 Confusion Ray
  • The tooltip for this ability states it applies  Befuddled for 3 turns.
 Corrosive Spit
  • This action lacks the IsHarmful spell flag, and as such is able to target creatures affected by  Sanctuary.
 Create Sorcery Points
  • This feature can be used to get nearly unlimited sorcery points using bugs that allow you to obtain infinite uses of Freecast (as detailed on its page).
 Crushing Flight (Owlbear Wild Shape)
  • Rather than taking half damage on save (which would be (2d8 + bonus damage)/2Bludgeoning), targets instead take (1d8 + bonus damage)/2Bludgeoning which is closer to one quarter damage.
    • This damage is always dealt as magical, regardless whether or not the attacker has  Primal Strike.
 Cutting Words
  • The visual effect and reaction spell are always directed towards the source of the attack, whether the attack has an attack roll or a saving throw. As a result, when Cutting Words is used to the reduce the saving throw roll of an enemy against a spell cast by a non-enemy creature, the visual effect and reaction spell will still be directed towards the caster.
    • The reaction spell is flagged as a harmful spell, and if the caster is a neutral creature it may become hostile towards the bard and its party.
  • Despite being flagged with HasVerbalComponent, Cutting Words may be used even while silenced.
  • Cutting Words is missing the potency of the bardic dice in its description when displayed in the combat log.
  • Cutting Words checks for the bard level of the source of the attack, instead of the bard that is using Cutting Words (observer). As a result, unless the attacker is also a bard, the maximum difference in roll value that Cutting Words can trigger on is 6 instead of the expected 8 or 10 for bards that are level 5 or above.
 Dawnburst Strike
  • The description in-game notes an incorrect  DC 13 Constitution Saving Throw save. It requires a weapon action save with a +2 DC bonus.
  • Despite the in-game description stating only enemies in the light must save against becoming blinded, the blindness affects all creatures in the area, even allies.
    • Due to a coding error, blindness does not affect the original target of the attack.
  • The additional ⁠Radiant damage is treated as a separate damage rider source even in Honour Mode.
 Dazzling Breath
  • When receiving this action via Starry Form, it is not properly granted with Wisdom as its spellcasting modifier. The damage therefore uses the spellcasting modifier of the most recently acquired class. The DC, however, always uses the Constitution modifier.
 Defensive Duellist
  • Unlike similar reactions (Shield Master: Block), the icon for Defensive Duellist in the reactions tab does not "gray out" when the reaction is unavailable due to an incompatible equipped weapon.
 Deflect Missiles
  • Damage does not need to be reduced to 0 in order to redirect the attack.
  • Against ranged attacks that fire multiple projectiles, such as  Multiattack (Ranged) or dual wielded Hand Crossbows, only the last attack can be deflected to reduce its damage. None of the projectiles can be thrown back with  Deflect Missiles: Redirect.
 Destructive Wrath
  • Destructive Wrath will trigger when casting the lightning or thunder variants of  Glyph of Warding, but the damage of the ward explosion is unaffected.
  • The reaction will also trigger when casting some spells which deal no damage.'"`UNIQ--ref-00009930-QINU`"' Destructive Wrath will be wasted if used on these spells:
    •  Bolts of Doom
    •  Bone-shaking Thunder
    •  Conjure Elemental: Air Elemental
    •  Conjure Elemental: Air Myrmidon
    •  Conjure Elemental: Earth Elemental
    •  Conjure Elemental: Earth Myrmidon
    •  Conjure Minor Elemental: Mud Mephits
    •  Planar Ally: Djinni
 Detonate
  • The tooltip says this attack deals 100Fire. This is incorrect as applied to creatures and the Overgrown Portcullis.
  • A sapper raised as a spore servant using  Animating Spores only deals 2d6Force and 2d6Fire, with a saving throw to negate the fire damage (the equivalent of a smokepowder surface igniting)
 Dip
  • Weapons can be dipped into a  Flaming Sphere only if it was created by a non-upcasted  Flaming Sphere spell.
 Dirty Trick: Flick o' the Wrist
  • This action does not trigger on-hit weapon functors found on many weapons, such as  Sussur Dagger.
 Dirty Trick: Sand Toss
  • When used with a ranged weapon currently active, the attack roll uses the strength modifier.
  • Since this action makes a melee weapon attack roll, it receives -5 penalty from  Great Weapon Master: All In but its damage does not increase by 10 when wielding Two-Handed and Versatile (no shield) weapons.
 Divine Intervention: Opulent Revival
  • This does not restore any of the new class resources added in Patch 8.
  • Hit points are restored to characters based on the maximum hit points of the caster, not the affected character.
 Divine Smite
  • The  Level 1 Spell Slot version of this action changes attack animations in Honour mode due to an override in the code.
  • The  Level 4 Spell Slot,  Level 5 Spell Slot, and  Level 6 Spell Slot versions of this action do not lose DRS in Honour mode when used as an attack, while the equivalent reaction versions do.
 Divine Strike: Cold (Melee)
  • This attack is not correctly marked with a cold DamageType flag, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for cold damage.
 Divine Strike: Cold (Ranged)
  • When wielding two Hand Crossbows and Dual Wielding toggle enabled, this attack will consume both an  Action and  Bonus Action, but the offhand attack will not be performed.
 Divine Strike: Fire (Melee)
  • This attack is not correctly marked with a fire DamageType flag, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for fire damage.
 Divine Strike: Fire (Ranged)
  • When wielding two Hand Crossbows and Dual Wielding toggle enabled, this attack will consume both an  Action and  Bonus Action, but the offhand attack will not be performed.
 Divine Strike: Lightning (Melee)
  • This attack is not correctly marked with a lightning DamageType flag, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for lightning damage.
 Divine Strike: Lightning (Ranged)
  • When wielding two Hand Crossbows and Dual Wielding toggle enabled, this attack will consume both an  Action and  Bonus Action, but the offhand attack will not be performed.
 Divine Strike: Necrotic (Melee)
  • This attack is not correctly marked with a necrotic DamageType flag, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for necrotic damage such as Malefic Funghi.
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to struck targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy.
 Divine Strike: Necrotic (Ranged)
  • When wielding two Hand Crossbows and Dual Wielding toggle is enabled, this attack consumes both an  Action and  Bonus Action, but the offhand attack does not occur.
  • This attack is incorrectly marked with a piercing DamageType flag, rather than necrotic, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for necrotic damage such as  Malefic Funghi.
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to struck targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy.
 Divine Strike: Poison (Melee)
  • This attack is not correctly marked with a poison DamageType flag, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for poison damage.
 Divine Strike: Radiant (Melee)
  • This attack is not correctly marked with a radiant DamageType flag, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for radiant damage.
 Divine Strike: Radiant (Ranged)
  • When wielding two Hand Crossbows and Dual Wielding toggle enabled, this attack will consume both an  Action and  Bonus Action, but the offhand attack will not be performed.
 Divine Strike: Thunder (Melee)
  • This attack is not correctly marked with a thunder DamageType flag, which means it does not trigger certain effects which check for thunder damage, most notably  Destructive Wrath.
 Divine Strike: Thunder (Ranged)
  • When wielding two Hand Crossbows and Dual Wielding toggle enabled, this attack will consume both an  Action and  Bonus Action, but the offhand attack will not be performed.
 Divine Strike: Weapon (Melee)
  • This attack deals non-magical damage when used as an  Action, but deals magical damage when used as a post-strike  Reaction.
    • Due to a coding mistake, when used as a post-strike reaction in Honour Mode this attack deals non-magical damage.
 Divine Strike: Weapon (Ranged)
  • When wielding two Hand Crossbows and Dual Wielding toggle enabled, this attack consumes both an  Action and  Bonus Action, but the offhand attack is not performed.
  • This attack deals non-magical damage when used as an action, but deals magical damage when used as a post-strike reaction.
 Diving Strike
  • If this attack misses and  Reckless Attack is triggered in response, the attack roll is not actually rerolled, so it will always still miss. However, if Reckless Attack is already active, the attack roll is made with  Advantage as expected.
 Drunken Technique
  • This attack does not trigger Cloak of Cunning Brume despite granting the benefits of  Disengage.
 Edge of Darkness
  • The in-game tooltip for this action is inaccurate and missing key information about it being an AoE attack.
  • The tooltip claims there is an associated  Constitution Saving Throw, but this is not true.
 End Rage
  • This action lacks a Self() restriction, and can be used to remove Rage effects from other characters albeit at a very close range.
 Enrage
  • Due to a coding error, Owlbear's Rage may not be removed from the Druid if Owlbear form is lost.
 Enraged Throw
  • Unlike with an ordinary  Throw, throwing  Boo with enraged throw will not  Blind the target.
 Entropic Ward
  • This reaction cannot be used while affected by  Starry Form or when  Disguised.
 Evasive Footwork
  • The 1 turn duration of  Evasive Footwork is deceptively short. The duration ticks down at the end of the Battle Master's turn and upon doing so immediately ends. Thus, aside from opportunity attacks or ripostes made during the user's active turn, Evasive Footwork ends before any enemies make their attacks.
  • This action lacks a Self() restriction, and can provide its effect to other characters – albeit at a very close range.
 Exposing Bite
  • This condition is removed after any attack roll against the affected creature within 3 m (10 ft), but the critical hit only applies if it is made within 2 m (7 ft). This means the effect is wasted when attacking an affected creature with an extra reach weapon from maximum range.
 Fangs of the Fire Snake
  • Despite the description, ranged weapon attacks are also increased in damage for the duration but not any spells which are also melee attacks, such as  Touch of the Storm.
 Fear Ray
  • The tooltip for this ability states it applies  Frightened for 3 turns.
 Fey Presence: Beguiling
  • This spell is not affected by effects which provide advantage or disadvantage on saving throws against being  Charmed. Instead it is affected by those which provide advantage or disadvantage on saving throws against being  Frightened (e.g.,  Shield of the Undevout).
 Fiendish Flameblast
  • The spell description states it should apply  Infernal Burning, but it instead applies  Burning (Orthonic).
 Fierce Perilous Stakes
  • This can be cast multiple times on the same target to apply multiple instances of  Fierce Perilous Stakes at once, and can even stack with  Perilous Stakes. The critical hit threshold reduction, bonus damage, and healing effect from each application all stack with each other. The damage vulnerability does not stack.
 Firewine Explosion
  • On save, targets take (4d6)/2Fire damage instead of (2d6)/2Fire damage which is effectively full damage.
 Fist of Four Thunders
  • This spell is missing the trigger for  Martial Arts: Bonus Unarmed Strike, and will not grant its effect.
 Flurry of Moths: Attack
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to struck targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy.
 Flurry of Moths: Blinding Swarm
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy when a target successfully rolls a saving throw against this reaction.
 Flurry of Moths: Mighty Blinding Swarm
  • A hidden technical condition, which is responsible for applying a visual effect to targets, triggers the passives from  Boots of Stormy Clamour,  Coldbrim Hat, and  Diadem of Arcane Synergy when a target successfully rolls a saving throw against this reaction.
 Fly (Illithid Power)
  • While it is supposed to replace the Jump action's keybinding, this interaction is unreliable and seems to be bugged. It will often initially work, but then be reset to Jump when e.g. loading a saved game.
 Frenzied Strike
  • This attack no longer applies Frenzied Strain once the Barbarian reaches level 9.
 Frenzy
  • This version of Rage is usable when already affected by Rage once the Barbarian reaches level 9.
 Fungal Infestation
  • Fungal Infestation can create infinite zombies at the end of Act Two using the recovery station before the boss fight to regain charges paired with being able to raise an Intellect Devourer even after their corpse has been used.
 Gale (class action)
  • The tooltip incorrectly states this requires a Strength save. The correct Dexterity save is listed above.
 Gargantuan Cleave
  • The tooltip shows this action applying full weapon damage when in fact it deals half the weapon damage.
 Goading Attack (Melee)
  • The target has  Disadvantage on all attacks, even against the goading attacker.
